paths.description: Homepage and recommendation catalogue; entry, navigation, consent, responsive, performance, privacy, and preference conditions.
Top/all listing template representing catalogue browsing and prices.
Representative book detail and commercial/read entry path.
Invalid route to assess HTTP and recovery behavior.

findings.summary: Layout adapts to narrow viewports with no horizontal overflow and no fixed pixel widths forcing a desktop layout on mobile; viewport meta present; fluid scaling and intrinsic sizing rather than brittle breakpoints.
findings.evidence: At a requested 360x800 viewport the book-detail page forced a 970 CSS-pixel viewport and rendered a tiny desktop layout; meta viewport is width=970.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace width=970 with width=device-width and reflow the legacy book template responsively.

findings.summary: The representative primary flow can be completed end-to-end with predictable steps, no avoidable dead ends, no hidden required information, and no needless detours through modals, account walls, or upsells.
findings.evidence: The representative browse-to-book path lands on a 970 px legacy detail template at mobile width, making the reading/purchase interface extremely small and difficult to operate.
findings.suggestedFix: Unify the book/read/purchase journey on the responsive application shell and test it at narrow widths.

findings.summary: Text is legible and inclusively rendered: comfortable line layout, precise alignment, stable rendering across mixed fonts, no clipping or cramped wrapping that harms comprehension.
findings.evidence: The 360 px book capture is a 970 px desktop page scaled down, producing text and controls too small for comfortable reading.
findings.suggestedFix: Reflow book detail at device width with readable type sizes and line lengths.

findings.summary: Honours prefers-reduced-motion: non-essential animations and auto-advance are reduced or removed when the user asks for less motion.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, 155 animations were still running with 1200 ms duration.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable or greatly shorten non-essential carousel/card animations under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

findings.summary: No intrusive pop-ups, interstitials or banners that obscure content on load; overlays are dismissible and content-first.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile load screenshots show a cookie/recommendation banner obscuring a substantial portion of content before interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not cover content on load; use a compact, accessible consent surface with clear choices.

findings.summary: Touch targets are adequately sized and hover-only affordances have a non-hover fallback, and keyboard focus is visible, so the UI works for touch, pointer and keyboard alike.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found six target-size failures, seven unnamed buttons, and seven unnamed links; the DOM probe also found 24x24 and 34x36 controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Name icon controls, provide visible focus, and make targets at least 44 CSS px where practical.

findings.summary: Core Web Vitals are in the good range: LCP is fast, interaction latency (INP) is low, and CLS is minimal; work is prioritised and deferred sensibly.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured home LCP 16.47 s and TBT 672 ms; book LCP 10.87 s, CLS 0.187, and TBT 313.5 ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP image/content, defer non-critical scripts, and reduce blocking work.

findings.summary: No cumulative layout shift from late content (images, banners, fonts) that arrives without reserved space.
findings.evidence: Mobile layout observer measured home CLS 0.388 and book CLS 0.116; 17 images lacked explicit dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve image/banner space with dimensions or aspect-ratio and prevent late recommendation shifts.

findings.summary: The main thread is not blocked by long tasks or heavy scripting; work is deferred, chunked, prioritised, or moved off-thread.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 672 ms TBT on home; trace recorded five long tasks and 97.88 ms TBT in its separate capture.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer analytics and split/prioritise application work to remove long tasks and TBT.

findings.summary: Critical resources are delivered efficiently: cache headers are useful, render-blocking chains are short, fonts do not block or shift text, HTTP delivery is modern, and network dependency trees do not delay the main content.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 154 requests and 6.58 MB transferred, with several parser-inserted scripts and missing cache/compression signals.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve responsive modern hero images, preload only the actual LCP asset, and defer non-critical scripts.

findings.summary: The page does not ship large unused or duplicated JavaScript/CSS, avoidable legacy bundles, or third-party code that dominates the load without user value.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 778,059 bytes of unused JavaScript and HAR recorded 41 script requests totalling 1.98 MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unused application/third-party JS and load optional analytics only after consent/need.

findings.summary: Interactive elements have accessible names, correct roles, and form fields have labels; images have alt text where meaningful; canvas/expressive content is exposed to assistive technology.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found seven unnamed buttons and seven unnamed links on home; book probe found 34 images without alt text.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accessible names to icon controls/links and meaningful alt text to book-detail images.

findings.summary: Heading and landmark structure is logical, focus order follows reading order, keyboard focus is always visible, and interactive state survives DOM moves.
findings.evidence: Home has no h1 or main landmark and starts at h3; book has no main landmark and Lighthouse flagged heading order.
findings.suggestedFix: Add one main landmark, a page h1, logical heading levels, and verified visible keyboard focus order.

findings.summary: The experience remains usable when zoomed or reflowed, touch targets are large enough, media has captions or equivalents where needed, and the viewport does not prevent user scaling.
findings.evidence: Home viewport sets maximum-scale=1; book uses width=970, and Lighthouse failed meta-viewport and target-size checks.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale=1/fixed viewport constraints and make content reflow and targets usable when zoomed.

findings.summary: Served over HTTPS with a sensible Content-Security-Policy and secure, SameSite cookies; no mixed content or obvious transport/header smells.
findings.evidence: HTTPS and HSTS are present, but CSP and X-Content-Type-Options are absent and 24 of 31 observed cookies lack Secure.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a tested CSP, nosniff, and Secure/SameSite cookie defaults.

findings.summary: No over-collection of user data, no leaky third parties, and analytics/background data collection is minimised and batched rather than chatty or session-wide by default.
findings.evidence: Tracker capture found 20 third-party origins and four known tracker domains; HAR shows 73 third-party requests and 5.89 MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate analytics, delay it until consent, and remove trackers not tied to user value.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defenses are configured where appropriate: HSTS, clickjacking protection (frame-ancestors / X-Frame-Options), Trusted Types for XSS-sensitive apps, origin isolation, privacy-preserving third-party cookie posture, and sensible Referrer-Policy / Permissions-Policy.
findings.evidence: Headers lacked frame protection, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, CSP/frame-ancestors, and X-Content-Type-Options.
findings.suggestedFix: Add CSP frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, nosniff, and appropriate isolation.

findings.summary: No deceptive design: no confirmshaming, forced continuity, disguised ads, or nagging consent walls; honest defaults; clear pricing and consent; easy reversal/cancel; predictable, declaratively-wired actions; and no hidden-text tricks (hidden content stays deep-linkable and indexable rather than used to deceive).
findings.evidence: The on-load consent banner offers only “Принять”; it states continued use constitutes agreement and provides no equally visible reject choice.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide equally clear accept/reject choices and do not treat continued browsing as consent.

findings.summary: Checkout, subscription, consent, authentication and account-management flows are clear, reversible, and proportionate: pricing and commitments are visible, cancellation is findable, sensitive actions re-authenticate when appropriate, and users are not tricked into continuity.
findings.evidence: Book purchase content is rendered through the fixed 970 px mobile template, while consent is one-sided; clear, proportionate mobile commercial interaction is not achieved.
findings.suggestedFix: Make pricing, consent, purchase, cancellation, and account actions clear and responsive.

findings.summary: Images and decorative assets are optimised and served at appropriate resolutions; decorative pseudo-element imagery and heavy decorative images are resolution-optimised rather than oversized.
findings.evidence: HAR transferred 4.48 MB of images; three hero JPGs are 0.84–0.97 MB each, six images are oversized, and 23 use legacy formats.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP responsive variants and stop sending 1920 px, near-1 MB banners to small screens.

findings.summary: Background work and fetching are not wasteful: background processing is efficient and de-prioritised, and the lightest technique that achieves the result is preferred over heavy or redundant work.
findings.evidence: The page starts 41 scripts and 73 third-party requests on load, including multiple analytics/tag-manager stacks; Lighthouse estimates 778 KB unused JS.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove redundant analytics and defer background collection until idle, consented, and necessary.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts, fonts, video, audio, animation and heavy media are proportionate to the user value they provide; autoplay or background media is avoided unless essential and resource use is cached or deferred where possible.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 5.89 MB from third-party origins and trackers reported 20 third-party origins, disproportionate for a book-listing first view.
findings.suggestedFix: Set and enforce third-party request/byte budgets; lazy-load optional integrations.

findings.summary: Honours prefers-color-scheme: a usable dark mode exists and is driven by the user's preference (color-scheme / prefers-color-scheme / light-dark()), not hard-coded light only.
findings.evidence: Dark emulation screenshot stayed on the same white surfaces as the default capture; no color-scheme feature was found in captured CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Add color-scheme: light dark and retint surfaces with prefers-color-scheme/light-dark().

findings.summary: Overlays and rich controls use the right primitive: popover (with declarative light-dismiss) for transient UI, dialog for modal flows, details for disclosure, native-but-branded selects and pickers, rather than ad-hoc divs.
findings.evidence: DOM probe found zero dialog, popover, and details elements while the on-load consent overlay is implemented as custom chrome.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog/popover semantics, focus management, and declarative dismissal for overlays.

findings.summary: Text and essential UI meet WCAG colour-contrast minimums against their background.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported 27 color-contrast failures on the home page.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust low-contrast text and control tokens to meet WCAG contrast minimums.

findings.summary: Valid doctype and charset, images sized with correct aspect ratio, no deprecated APIs misused, and CSS/HTML are well structured and not needlessly repetitive. (HTTPS, CSP and permission hygiene are judged under be-private-and-secure, not here.)
findings.evidence: Although doctype/UTF-8 are valid, 17 images lack dimensions, six are oversized, and 23 use legacy raster formats.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic dimensions, correct aspect ratios, responsive sources, and modern formats.

findings.summary: The page uses the platform cleanly: no deprecated APIs, no avoidable BFCache blockers, no broken source maps or inspector issues, no stale vulnerable libraries, no paste-prevention on inputs, and no notification/geolocation prompts on load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found deprecated API use, missing source maps, DevTools inspector issues, a BFCache blocker on book detail, and third-party cookie issues.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove deprecated calls/BFCache blockers, ship valid source maps, and resolve DevTools issues.

findings.summary: Links are crawlable (real href), there is a viewport meta tag, robots does not block indexing, and link text is descriptive.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found a non-crawlable anchor and unnamed links; book detail uses a fixed width=970 viewport instead of a mobile-friendly viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real named href links and a device-width scalable viewport on every template.

findings.summary: Where the site is an app, it is installable (web app manifest) and offers an offline fallback and works on flaky networks. (Contextual: a brochure or intrinsically-online site may reasonably not need this.)
findings.evidence: The app-like reading service links a web manifest, but the loaded home page had no active service-worker controller or demonstrated offline fallback.
findings.suggestedFix: Register a service worker with a tested offline reading/navigation fallback or clarify non-offline behavior.

findings.summary: Repeating a representative interaction (open/close a modal, navigate a route and back, infinite-scroll a list) about 10 times does not grow retained heap without bound; what is allocated during the interaction is released when it ends.
findings.evidence: After ten bottom/top scroll cycles, heap summary grew from 45.30 MB/784,915 nodes to 50.23 MB/839,991 nodes (about 10.9% bytes and 7.0% nodes); separate-session variance lowers confidence.
findings.suggestedFix: Repeat in one controlled session with forced GC and listener instrumentation; then remove retained scroll/listener/cache growth.

findings.summary: State and route changes use View Transitions (including same-document, cross-document and scroll-driven/staggered) rather than instant, jarring swaps.
findings.evidence: Rendered DOM/CSS contained no view-transition usage; navigation crosses visibly different Angular and legacy templates without a shared transition treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Add same/cross-document View Transitions to meaningful route and state changes with a no-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Sticky/affixed UI reacts to scroll state and position (e.g. the new scroll-state(scrolled) query, shrinking headers, progress indicators) so chrome responds to position instead of static or JS-driven toggling.
findings.evidence: The long 5,774 px home page retained static navigation chrome and captured CSS had no scroll-state query or scroll timeline.
findings.suggestedFix: Use scroll-state/container queries or a lightweight progress treatment to orient long-page navigation.

findings.summary: Navigation and in-page jumps guide attention (highlight effects, scroll/carousel markers, directional transitions, drill-down and drawer navigation) so the user can follow where focus moved.
findings.evidence: The sampled home/list/detail transitions provide no directional transition, progress marker, current-location trail, or post-navigation attention cue.
findings.suggestedFix: Add current-location and directional cues when moving between catalogue, author, and book views.

findings.summary: Components adapt to their container with container queries (incl. anchored container queries) and content/state-based styling where reused at different sizes, not only global viewport breakpoints.
findings.evidence: Captured CSS reported zero container-query rules; reused book/card components rely on template/viewport treatment rather than container-level adaptation.
findings.suggestedFix: Make reused cards container-query aware rather than binding all adaptation to templates/viewports.

findings.summary: Permission prompts are requested in context (not on load), and authentication uses modern, phishing-resistant methods (passkeys / WebAuthn) where relevant rather than passwords alone.
findings.evidence: No permission prompt appeared on load, but the public login affordance had no WebAuthn/passkey capability visible in loaded scripts or sampled auth entry points.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey/WebAuthn sign-in and request permissions only after explicit user action.

taskList.title: Replace width=970 with width=device-width and reflow the legacy book template responsively.
Unify the book/read/purchase journey on the responsive application shell and test it at narrow widths.
Reflow book detail at device width with readable type sizes and line lengths.
Disable or greatly shorten non-essential carousel/card animations under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.
Do not cover content on load; use a compact, accessible consent surface with clear choices.
Name icon controls, provide visible focus, and make targets at least 44 CSS px where practical.
Prioritise the LCP image/content, defer non-critical scripts, and reduce blocking work.
Reserve image/banner space with dimensions or aspect-ratio and prevent late recommendation shifts.
Defer analytics and split/prioritise application work to remove long tasks and TBT.
Serve responsive modern hero images, preload only the actual LCP asset, and defer non-critical scripts.
Remove unused application/third-party JS and load optional analytics only after consent/need.
Add accessible names to icon controls/links and meaningful alt text to book-detail images.
Add one main landmark, a page h1, logical heading levels, and verified visible keyboard focus order.
Remove maximum-scale=1/fixed viewport constraints and make content reflow and targets usable when zoomed.
Deploy a tested CSP, nosniff, and Secure/SameSite cookie defaults.
Consolidate analytics, delay it until consent, and remove trackers not tied to user value.
Add CSP frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, nosniff, and appropriate isolation.
Provide equally clear accept/reject choices and do not treat continued browsing as consent.
Make pricing, consent, purchase, cancellation, and account actions clear and responsive.
Generate AVIF/WebP responsive variants and stop sending 1920 px, near-1 MB banners to small screens.
Remove redundant analytics and defer background collection until idle, consented, and necessary.
Set and enforce third-party request/byte budgets; lazy-load optional integrations.
Add color-scheme: light dark and retint surfaces with prefers-color-scheme/light-dark().
Use dialog/popover semantics, focus management, and declarative dismissal for overlays.
Adjust low-contrast text and control tokens to meet WCAG contrast minimums.
Add intrinsic dimensions, correct aspect ratios, responsive sources, and modern formats.
Remove deprecated calls/BFCache blockers, ship valid source maps, and resolve DevTools issues.
Use real named href links and a device-width scalable viewport on every template.
Register a service worker with a tested offline reading/navigation fallback or clarify non-offline behavior.
Repeat in one controlled session with forced GC and listener instrumentation; then remove retained scroll/listener/cache growth.
Add same/cross-document View Transitions to meaningful route and state changes with a no-motion fallback.
Use scroll-state/container queries or a lightweight progress treatment to orient long-page navigation.
Add current-location and directional cues when moving between catalogue, author, and book views.
Make reused cards container-query aware rather than binding all adaptation to templates/viewports.
Offer passkey/WebAuthn sign-in and request permissions only after explicit user action.
